title: voice-driven-prompt-pipelines-proto-notebook
content:
Quick scratchpad for a voice-driven prompt pipeline prototype. Rough, verbal thinking — mostly notes to self and small sketches of API shapes + runtime flow. Goal: capture a minimal API that accepts audio (or pre-transcribed text) and composes an LLM prompt pipeline with hooks for transcription, intent extraction, and streaming token-level responses back to the client (audio or text).

Context / why:
- Several customers ask for low-latency voice assistants driven by our hosted API. They want simple client APIs and easy server-side pipeline wiring (transcribe -> canonicalize -> prompt -> model -> TTS).
- Need to support hybrid flows: client transcribes locally and sends text OR client sends raw audio. Also consider a fallback path for unreliable networks (client partial transcripts).
- This is a personal prototyping note; align later with Solutions Eng and SDK teams.

Non-goals:
- This is NOT the final production contract. No SLA commitments here. Focus on developer ergonomics and observable boundaries.

Key concepts / primitives:
- source.type: "audio" | "transcript" — origin of the input.
- transcription.hints: optional structured metadata (language, domain/context, grammar hints).
- pipeline.stages: ordered list of lightweight transforms (e.g., normalize, redact, enrich, prompt-template).
- response.mode: streaming | final — whether model tokens are streamed.
- output.delivery: text | audio | both (for client-side TTS).
- provenance: attach per-stage ids for traceability (useful for replay/QA).

Sketch: top-level request shape (pseudo-JSON in doc text):

REQUEST (POST /v1/voice/prompt-run):
{
  "request_id": "uuid",
  "source": {
    "type": "audio",              // "audio" or "transcript"
    "encoding": "opus/48000",    // optional when audio
    "chunks": ["base64-chunk-1", "base64-chunk-2"], // OR streaming boundary
    "transcript": null,           // optional if client pre-transcribed
    "hints": {
      "lang": "en-US",
      "domain": "support",
      "utterance_id": "client-uuid-123"
    }
  },
  "pipeline": {
    "stages": [
      {"id":"transcribe","type":"transcribe","params":{"model":"whisper-small"}},
      {"id":"normalize","type":"text-normalize","params":{"normalize_emails":true}},
      {"id":"intent","type":"intent-extractor","params":{"schema":"support-intent-v1"}},
      {"id":"prompt","type":"prompt-template","params":{"template_id":"support-quick-reply"}}
    ],
    "timeout_ms": 12000
  },
  "response": {"mode":"streaming","delivery":"text"},
  "client_context": {"user_id":"abc", "session_id":"s-123"}
}
Notes about the shape: keep the pipeline declarative. Each stage is a named plugin (could be internal function). This lets us route/replace implementations on the server (e.g., use a faster transcribe to meet latency SLOs).

Streaming variant notes:
- Client opens a bidi websocket or uses SSE to receive token deltas.
- We need per-event metadata: stage provenance, tokens, confidence, partial_transcript, audio-tts-chunk refs. Example event shape: {event_type:"partial_transcript", stage_id:"transcribe", text: "...", confidence:0.89, watermark_ms: 3450}.
- For audio-origin requests, early partial transcripts should be emitted asap (prefetch/k:v caching).

Server-side lifecycle (sequence):
- Receive request metadata (request_id + pipeline). If audio streaming: accept initial chunk and ack.
- Start transcribe stage (if audio). Emit partial_transcript events as available.
- After transcript (or if source.type==transcript), run normalize -> intent -> prompt. Each intermediate output should be attachable to the trace.
- Evaluate prompt with chosen model variant (support fallback to cheaper quantized variant if latency window missed).
- Stream generation tokens back. If response.delivery==audio, also concurrently synthesize TTS chunks and stream audio binary frames (or provide audio URIs).
- Finalize trace + cost accounting.

Config knobs we want exposed (developer-facing):
- latency_target_ms: e.g., 200ms partial, 1200ms complete. Used to pick transcribe/model variants.
- allow_partial_replies: true/false (controls early assistant replies based on partial transcripts).
- privacy.redact: list of redaction rules (emails, phone, SSN). Could be pre-transcribe or post-transcribe.
- tts_profile: "neutral" | "friendly" | "concise" (maps to voice model + prosody params).
- transcript_confidence_threshold: don't surface partials below this.

Open design questions / tradeoffs: 
- Should pipeline be fully declarative (list of names + params) or allow embedded code snippets (lambda-like)? Declarative is safer for routing & auditing but less flexible.
- How to handle billing? Charge for transcribe tokens + inference tokens + TTS bytes. Need to expose a cost estimate in the response header and in event stream so clients can present an ETA or pre-approve cost.
- Privacy / PII: where to enforce redaction? We should provide a 'redact_on_server' flag so customers can request PII removed before storing or sending to downstream. But server-side redaction increases latency.
- Multi-turn: do we provide conversation state glue (session memory) or require client to manage? Probably leave memory management to client for initial API; add optional session_id and memory cursors.

Example minimal flow (text-only client, shorter):
POST /v1/voice/prompt-run -> source.type=transcript -> pipeline: [normalize,prompt] -> response: streaming tokens.

Edge cases / failure modes: 
- Partial audio loss -> emit "incomplete_segment" event with last_watermark. Client can resend chunk or mark end-of-utterance.
- Long silence -> transcription model may output empty; pipeline should detect and cancel generation to save cost.
- Conflicting pipeline stage params (e.g., two different language hints) -> choose precedence: source.hints > stage.params > pipeline.default_params. Document this precedence.

Experimental teleport feature (brainstorm):
- client-side local ASR + server-side align: client sends local transcript + compressed audio fingerprint. Server can align local transcript to server transcript using fingerprint to improve timestamp alignment for TTS prosody. Might help lip-synced avatars. Complex - backburner.

Observability / Telemetry:
- Emit structured events into our tracing pipeline with tags: request_id, stage_id, user_id, token_count, latency_ms, fallback_used (true/false).
- Expose per-request debug bundle (on-demand) that includes intermediate transcripts, stage outputs, and model variant ids. Only available with consent.

Prototype priorities / ToDos:
- [ ] Spin up a tiny prototype server that accepts POST body above and returns streaming SSE events. Keep business logic simple: transcribe (call toy whisper), run a template prompt, call gpt-like model (hosted local) and stream back tokens. (Owner: me)
- [ ] Add a small client shim (JS) that can stream microphone chunks as base64 into the request and render SSE events -> text. (Owner: Jin)
- [ ] Add simple TTS playback example (browser audio) that consumes audio frames from SSE or fetches audio URL for final response. (Owner: Miguel)
- [ ] Draft a short README + sample SDK function for node/python. (Owner: me)

Notes-to-self:
- Keep the pipeline stage IDs small and stable; they become part of instrumentation and logs.
- Keep default pipeline minimal for discovery: [transcribe, prompt]. Extra stages opt-in.
- Consider idempotency: request_id used for dedupe for retried uploads. Persist minimal state until finalization to avoid double-billing.

Rough performance targets for prototype (benchmarks to measure):
- Partial transcript latency <= 300ms for 1s audio chunks (local + server combined) on hosted small model.
- First token of assistant within 800ms of utterance end for simple queries.
- TTS chunk playback continuous (no gaps) for streaming audio responses.

Example SSE event sequence (text):
- event: partial_transcript
  data: {"stage":"transcribe","text":"i need help with my password","confidence":0.87}
- event: stage_output
  data: {"stage":"intent","output":{"intent":"reset_password","slots":{}}}
- event: assistant_token
  data: {"token":"Reset ","seq":1}
- event: assistant_token
  data: {"token":"your ","seq":2}
- event: tts_chunk
  data: {"url":"https://s3/.../chunk-1.opus","seq":1}
- event: final
  data: {"cost_estimate":"$0.012","final_transcript":"...","duration_ms":1234}

Implementation notes (internal):
- Reuse existing transcribe connectors (whisper family) and our model API for generation. Add a small shim to convert stage outputs into model.input.
- For streaming tokens, piggyback our existing streaming infra (SSE / websocket) with a special event namespace for voice. Keep backward compatibility: streaming tokens use the same token format as text endpoints.

References / links:
- See early sketch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/voice-protos/pull/54
- Related Jira: INFR-4921 (voice pipelines experiment)

Random scribbles:
- Maybe add a "voice_profile_hint" that suggests grammar/tone (e.g., allow contractions) — useful for TTS + prompt template.
- Consider a small sample-rate-aware chunk size recommendation for mobile (200-800ms chunks).

End of scratchpad. Revisit after prototype.

-- Asha
